name: EOP Model
description: The EOP Model provides a structured approach to assessing organisational process capability. It combinestwo levels of analysis. First, it examines the organisational conditions that enable or constrain theunderstanding, ownership, management and continuous development of processes. Second, it examineshow this capability is manifested in selected individual processes. The organisational level comprises fivedimensions and the process level six dimensions. Using defined assessment anchors, each dimension isassigned to one of four ordinal maturity stages: unclear, informal, regulated or effectively managed.The EOP assessment does not produce a metric score. Its core result is a qualitatively justified dimensionalprofile. The numbers 1 to 4 serve solely as ordered labels for ordinal categories and must not beinterpreted as equidistant measurements. Arithmetic means and mathematically derived overall maturitylevels are therefore not part of the binding assessment logic. An optional EOP profile code may present thedimensional ratings compactly, but it does not replace either the complete profile or its qualitative rationale.This manual describes the purpose, structure, assessment logic, application and limitations of the model. Itprovides assessment anchors, documentation templates and an illustrative example. In Version 1.0, theEOP Model is to be understood as a conceptual and practice-oriented assessment and developmentmodel.
